children: Restarting reactors shut after a 2011 disaster could double atomic power’s share of total output to 20%, reducing fossil fuel imports. But it’s a glacial process. Access to Tokyo’s $2 trln spending plan could speed it up and even hasten the country’s broader energy transition.
Follow Hudson Lockett on Bluesky and X.

Japanese imports hit a monthly record of 12.1 trillion yen ($79 billion) in July, official data released on August 20 showed, as the value of crude oil purchases jumped 88% from a year ago thanks to elevated prices and larger shipments from the United States.
